subproblems.title: Smooth step profile on ℝ: 1 on (−∞, 1/2], 0 on [1, ∞), values in [0, 1], 3-Lipschitz
subproblems.statement: There is a C^infinity function φ : R → R such that (i) 0 <= φ(t) <= 1 for every t; (ii) φ(t) = 1 for every t <= 1/2; (iii) φ(t) = 0 for every t >= 1; (iv) φ is 3-Lipschitz, i.e. |φ(s) − φ(t)| <= 3|s − t| for all s, t ∈ R.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∃ φ : ℝ → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ ∧ (∀ t, 0 ≤ φ t ∧ φ t ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ t, t ≤ 1 / 2 → φ t = 1) ∧ (∀ t, 1 ≤ t → φ t = 0) ∧ LipschitzWith 3 φ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–3 of the supplied proof of the selected cutoff lemma aal_l1th_exists_cutoff. That is the explicit profile behind Simon's choice "|∇ζ| ≤ 3/ρ" (Ch. 5, proof of Lemma 2.1, p. 108); the book itself gives no construction. The supplied step 3(a) records only that φ is C^1. Step 3(b) below fills in the detail that the same φ is C^∞, which is what this child asserts; the selected parent later uses only C^1. This statement is the exact frozen type of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.exists_smooth_step_profile_lipschitz_three, reused unchanged. In Lean, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ means C^∞ (C^k for every finite k). LipschitzWith 3 φ (with 3 : ℝ≥0) means |φ(s) − φ(t)| ≤ 3|s − t| for all s, t.

Notation. Let S := Real.smoothTransition. Mathlib (Analysis/SpecialFunctions/SmoothTransition.lean) gives:
- S is C^∞ (Real.smoothTransition.contDiff);
- 0 ≤ S ≤ 1 (Real.smoothTransition.nonneg, Real.smoothTransition.le_one);
- S(s) = 0 for s ≤ 0 (Real.smoothTransition.zero_of_nonpos);
- S(s) = 1 for s ≥ 1 (Real.smoothTransition.one_of_one_le).

1. The bump g. Define g : ℝ → ℝ by g(t) := S(12(t − 1/2)) · S(12(1 − t)).
 (a) g is C^∞. The maps t ↦ 12(t − 1/2) and t ↦ 12(1 − t) are affine, hence C^∞. Composing them with S and multiplying the two factors keeps C^∞ (ContDiff.comp, ContDiff.mul). In particular g is continuous, so it is interval-integrable on every interval (Continuous.intervalIntegrable).
 (b) 0 ≤ g(t) ≤ 1 for every t, as a product of two numbers in [0, 1].
 (c) If t ≤ 1/2, then 12(t − 1/2) ≤ 0, so the first factor is 0 and g(t) = 0. If t ≥ 1, then 12(1 − t) ≤ 0, so the second factor is 0 and g(t) = 0.
 (d) If 7/12 ≤ t ≤ 11/12, then 12(t − 1/2) ≥ 12 · (1/12) = 1 and 12(1 − t) ≥ 12 · (1/12) = 1. Both factors equal 1, so g(t) = 1.

2. The constant c := ∫_{1/2}^{1} g(s) ds.
 - g is interval-integrable on each piece, so additivity of the interval integral (intervalIntegral.integral_add_adjacent_intervals, applied twice) gives
 c = ∫_{1/2}^{7/12} g + ∫_{7/12}^{11/12} g + ∫_{11/12}^{1} g.
 - The first and third integrals are ≥ 0, because g ≥ 0 by 1(b) and their bounds are in increasing order (intervalIntegral.integral_nonneg).
 - By 1(d), g = 1 on [7/12, 11/12], so the middle integral equals ∫_{7/12}^{11/12} 1 ds = 11/12 − 7/12 = 1/3 (intervalIntegral.integral_congr).
 - Hence c ≥ 1/3. In particular c > 0 and 0 < c⁻¹ ≤ 3.
 (Alternatively, intervalIntegral.integral_mono_interval, with 1/2 ≤ 7/12 ≤ 11/12 ≤ 1 and g ≥ 0, gives ∫_{7/12}^{11/12} g ≤ c directly.)

3. The profile. Put F(t) := ∫_{1/2}^{t} g(s) ds (oriented interval integral) and φ(t) := 1 − c⁻¹ F(t).
 (a) Derivative.
 - g is continuous, so the fundamental theorem of calculus (Continuous.integral_hasStrictDerivAt, or intervalIntegral.integral_hasDerivAt_right) gives HasDerivAt F (g(t)) t for every real t.
 - Hence HasDerivAt φ (−c⁻¹ g(t)) t for every t. So φ is differentiable on ℝ and deriv φ = −c⁻¹ · g as functions.
 (b) φ is C^∞.
 - By contDiff_infty_iff_deriv, a function ℝ → ℝ is C^∞ iff it is differentiable and its derivative is C^∞.
 - φ is differentiable by (a).
 - deriv φ = −c⁻¹ · g is a constant multiple of the C^∞ function g (1(a)), so it is C^∞.
 - Hence φ is C^∞. (Equivalently, F is C^∞ by the same criterion, since F is differentiable with deriv F = g, and φ = 1 − c⁻¹F.)
 (c) φ is 3-Lipschitz.
 - For every t, |deriv φ(t)| = c⁻¹ g(t) ≤ c⁻¹ · 1 ≤ 3, by 1(b) and step 2.
 - φ is differentiable and |deriv φ| ≤ 3 everywhere, so the mean value inequality (lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_deriv_le with C = 3) gives |φ(s) − φ(t)| ≤ 3|s − t| for all s, t.
 (d) Case t ≤ 1/2.
 - Every s between t and 1/2 satisfies s ≤ 1/2, so g(s) = 0 by 1(c).
 - Hence F(t) = ∫_{1/2}^{t} g = 0 (intervalIntegral.integral_congr with the zero function on [t, 1/2]).
 - So φ(t) = 1 − c⁻¹ · 0 = 1.
 (e) Case t ≥ 1.
 - By additivity, F(t) = ∫_{1/2}^{1} g + ∫_{1}^{t} g.
 - Here ∫_{1/2}^{1} g = c, and ∫_{1}^{t} g = 0 because g(s) = 0 for every s ∈ [1, t] by 1(c).
 - So F(t) = c and φ(t) = 1 − c⁻¹c = 0, since c ≠ 0.
 (f) Case 1/2 ≤ t ≤ 1.
 - g ≥ 0 and 1/2 ≤ t give F(t) ≥ 0 (intervalIntegral.integral_nonneg).
 - g ≥ 0 and [1/2, t] ⊆ [1/2, 1] give F(t) ≤ ∫_{1/2}^{1} g = c (intervalIntegral.integral_mono_interval).
 - Multiplying by c⁻¹ > 0 gives 0 ≤ c⁻¹F(t) ≤ c⁻¹c = 1, so 0 ≤ φ(t) ≤ 1.
 Every real t satisfies t ≤ 1/2, t ≥ 1, or 1/2 ≤ t ≤ 1. In the first two cases φ(t) ∈ {1, 0} by (d) and (e). Hence 0 ≤ φ(t) ≤ 1 for every real t.

4. Conclusion. φ satisfies every property in the statement:
 - C^∞, by 3(b);
 - values in [0, 1], by 3(f);
 - φ(t) = 1 for every t ≤ 1/2, by 3(d);
 - φ(t) = 0 for every t ≥ 1, by 3(e);
 - 3-Lipschitz, by 3(c). ∎
(Remark: in fact c = 5/12, but only c ≥ 1/3 is used.)
proof_key_steps: With S = Real.smoothTransition, g(t) = S(12(t − 1/2)) · S(12(1 − t)) is C^∞, 0 ≤ g ≤ 1, g = 0 for t ≤ 1/2 and for t ≥ 1, and g = 1 on [7/12, 11/12].
c = ∫_{1/2}^{1} g, split into three adjacent pieces, is ≥ ∫_{7/12}^{11/12} 1 = 1/3; so c > 0 and c⁻¹ ≤ 3.
φ(t) = 1 − c⁻¹ ∫_{1/2}^{t} g satisfies HasDerivAt φ (−c⁻¹ g(t)) t by the FTC; deriv φ = −c⁻¹ g is C^∞, so φ is C^∞ (contDiff_infty_iff_deriv).
|deriv φ| = c⁻¹ g ≤ c⁻¹ ≤ 3, so φ is 3-Lipschitz (lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_deriv_le).
φ = 1 for t ≤ 1/2, since g = 0 on [t, 1/2]. φ = 0 for t ≥ 1, by additivity and g = 0 on [1, t]. 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1 on [1/2, 1], since 0 ≤ ∫_{1/2}^{t} g ≤ c.

subproblems.title: The radial lift x ↦ φ(‖x − ξ‖/ρ) of a C^∞ profile with φ = 1 on (−∞, 1/2] is C^∞
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ N, ξ ∈ R^m (Euclidean space EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)), ρ > 0, and let φ : R → R be C^infinity with φ(t) = 1 for every t <= 1/2. Then the function ζ : R^m → R, ζ(x) := φ(‖x − ξ‖/ρ), is C^infinity.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (ξ : Rn m) (ρ : ℝ) (φ : ℝ → ℝ), 0 < ρ → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ → (∀ t, t ≤ 1 / 2 → φ t = 1) → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (fun x : Rn m => φ (‖x - ξ‖ / ρ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the supplied proof of the selected cutoff lemma aal_l1th_exists_cutoff ("ζ is C^1"). The radial function is smooth away from ξ because the Euclidean norm is smooth at nonzero vectors, and it is locally constant near ξ. Neither part of that argument depends on the order of smoothness. So it is stated here for a C^∞ profile with a C^∞ conclusion, and the profile is reduced to the two properties step 5 uses: φ is C^∞, and φ = 1 on (−∞, 1/2]. This statement is the exact frozen type of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.contDiff_radial_profile_of_eq_one_le_half, reused unchanged. The selected parent applies it to the profile of the sibling step_profile and weakens C^∞ to C^1. In Lean, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) means C^∞.

Hypotheses: m ∈ ℕ, ξ ∈ ℝ^m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), ρ > 0, φ : ℝ → ℝ is C^∞, and φ(t) = 1 for every t ≤ 1/2. Write ζ(x) := φ(‖x − ξ‖/ρ).

1. Reduction. By contDiff_iff_contDiffAt, ζ is C^∞ on ℝ^m iff it is C^∞ at every point x ∈ ℝ^m. Fix x. We treat the cases x = ξ and x ≠ ξ.

2. Case x = ξ.
 - ρ > 0, so ρ/2 > 0, and the open ball B°(ξ, ρ/2) = {y : ‖y − ξ‖ < ρ/2} is a neighbourhood of ξ (Metric.ball_mem_nhds).
 - For every y in this ball, dist(y, ξ) = ‖y − ξ‖ < ρ/2. Dividing by ρ > 0 gives ‖y − ξ‖/ρ < 1/2, in particular ≤ 1/2.
 - So the hypothesis on φ gives ζ(y) = φ(‖y − ξ‖/ρ) = 1. Thus ζ agrees with the constant function 1 on a neighbourhood of ξ.
 - Constant functions are C^∞ at every point (contDiffAt_const), and being C^∞ at a point depends only on the germ there (ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq). Hence ζ is C^∞ at ξ.

3. Case x ≠ ξ.
 - Then x − ξ ≠ 0, and the map y ↦ y − ξ is C^∞ (identity minus a constant).
 - On the real inner-product space ℝ^m the norm is C^∞ at every nonzero vector (contDiffAt_norm, valid for every smoothness order), in particular at x − ξ.
 - By the chain rule (ContDiffAt.comp, or ContDiffAt.norm), y ↦ ‖y − ξ‖ is C^∞ at x.
 - Dividing by the constant ρ keeps this (ContDiffAt.div_const). So h(y) := ‖y − ξ‖/ρ is C^∞ at x.
 - φ is C^∞ on all of ℝ, so the composite ζ = φ ∘ h is C^∞ at x (ContDiff.comp_contDiffAt).

4. Conclusion. Every x ∈ ℝ^m falls under step 2 or step 3. So ζ is C^∞ at every point, hence C^∞ on ℝ^m by step 1. (When m = 0, every point of ℝ^0 equals ξ, so only step 2 occurs.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to C^∞ at every point x (contDiff_iff_contDiffAt).
At x = ξ: ζ ≡ 1 on the open ball B°(ξ, ρ/2), a neighbourhood of ξ, because there ‖y − ξ‖/ρ < 1/2. So ζ is C^∞ at ξ (contDiffAt_const.congr_of_eventuallyEq).
At x ≠ ξ: y ↦ ‖y − ξ‖/ρ is C^∞ at x (contDiffAt_norm at x − ξ ≠ 0, chain rule, div_const). Composing with the C^∞ profile φ gives C^∞ at x.

subproblems.title: The radial lift of a K-Lipschitz profile has ‖Dζ(x)‖ ≤ K/ρ everywhere
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ N, ξ ∈ R^m (Euclidean space EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)), ρ > 0, K ∈ ℝ≥0, and let φ : R → R be K-Lipschitz, i.e. |φ(s) − φ(t)| <= K|s − t| for all s, t. Put ζ(y) := φ(‖y − ξ‖/ρ). Then for every x ∈ R^m the Fréchet derivative of ζ at x satisfies ‖Dζ(x)‖ <= K/ρ (operator norm). In Lean this is fderiv ℝ ζ x, which is 0 wherever ζ is not differentiable.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (ξ : Rn m) (ρ : ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0) (φ : ℝ → ℝ), 0 < ρ → LipschitzWith K φ → ∀ x : Rn m, ‖fderiv ℝ (fun y : Rn m => φ (‖y - ξ‖ / ρ)) x‖ ≤ (K : ℝ) / ρ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the supplied proof of the selected cutoff lemma aal_l1th_exists_cutoff, with the constant 3 replaced by an arbitrary Lipschitz constant K ∈ ℝ≥0. That step shows that ζ is (3/ρ)-Lipschitz, using the 3-Lipschitz profile (supplied step 3(b)) and the reverse triangle inequality, and then concludes ‖fderiv ℝ ζ x‖ ≤ 3/ρ by norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz. This statement is the exact frozen type of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.norm_fderiv_radial_profile_le_of_lipschitzWith, reused unchanged. The selected parent applies it with K = 3.

Hypotheses: m ∈ ℕ, ξ ∈ ℝ^m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), ρ > 0, K ∈ ℝ≥0, and φ : ℝ → ℝ is K-Lipschitz, i.e. |φ(s) − φ(t)| ≤ K|s − t| for all s, t. Put ζ(y) := φ(‖y − ξ‖/ρ).

1. Lipschitz estimate. Let y, w ∈ ℝ^m.
 - φ is K-Lipschitz and ρ > 0, so
 |ζ(y) − ζ(w)| ≤ K · |‖y − ξ‖/ρ − ‖w − ξ‖/ρ| = (K/ρ) · |‖y − ξ‖ − ‖w − ξ‖|.
 - The reverse triangle inequality (abs_norm_sub_norm_le) gives |‖y − ξ‖ − ‖w − ξ‖| ≤ ‖(y − ξ) − (w − ξ)‖ = ‖y − w‖ = dist(y, w).
 - Hence |ζ(y) − ζ(w)| ≤ (K/ρ) · dist(y, w).

2. Lipschitz constant. K/ρ ≥ 0, so step 1 says ζ is Lipschitz on ℝ^m with constant K/ρ. In Lean this is LipschitzWith (K / ρ.toNNReal) ζ, via LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul. The real value of K / ρ.toNNReal is (K : ℝ)/ρ, by NNReal.coe_div and Real.coe_toNNReal (ρ ≥ 0).

3. Derivative bound.
 - If a map between real normed spaces is C-Lipschitz, its Fréchet derivative has operator norm at most C at every point (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
 - At a point where the map is not differentiable, fderiv is 0 by convention, and the bound 0 ≤ C still holds.
 - Applying this to ζ with C = K/ρ from step 2 gives ‖fderiv ℝ ζ x‖ ≤ K/ρ for every x ∈ ℝ^m. ∎
proof_key_steps: |ζ(y) − ζ(w)| ≤ (K/ρ)|‖y − ξ‖ − ‖w − ξ‖| ≤ (K/ρ)‖y − w‖ (φ K-Lipschitz, ρ > 0, reverse triangle inequality).
So ζ is LipschitzWith (K / ρ.toNNReal), whose real value is K/ρ.
norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz gives ‖fderiv ℝ ζ x‖ ≤ K/ρ at every x (fderiv = 0 where ζ is not differentiable).
